newsitem.title: USA: Dun & Bradstreet sees rev, EPS growth in 96.
newsitem.headline: Dun & Bradstreet sees rev, EPS growth in 96.

text.p: Dun & Bradstreet Corp said on Thursday that after the spinoff of two of its segments, the "new" Dun & Bradstreet is expected to achieve earnings-per-share growth in the range of 3 to 4 percent in 1996 even after some expected operational weakness in the fourth quarter.
Revenues by the new company are expected to be in the mid-single digits for 1996, it said. The company also said it expects to maintain its $0.22 quarterly dividend through 1997.
Dun & Bradstreet is in the midst of splitting into three publicly traded companies: Cognizant Corp, ACNielsen, and a new Dun & Bradstreet Corp.

The new Dun & Bradstreet Corp will consist of D&B, a provider of commercial credit and business marketing information, and receivables management services; Moody's Investors Service, the debt rating agency and a major publisher of financial information for investors; and Reuben H. Donnelley, the independent marketer of Yellow Pages advertising in the United States.

The company's forecasts reflect some expected operational weakness in the fourth quarter, primarily due to flat directory sales at Reuben H. Donnelley and higher than anticipated start-up costs at Donnelley's new production facility in Raleigh, N.C.
In addition, Moody's fourth quarter revenue growth is expected to slow, reflecting the recent decline in corporate and public bond issue volumes, it said.
Dun & Bradstreet filed its Form 8-K with the Securities and Exchange Commission Thursday, one of the final steps in the reorganization process.
